assessment_summary: The statement is false. An attempt to prove it fails immediately because the worst-case time complexity for deterministic Quicksort with the first element as pivot occurs precisely on already-sorted (or reverse-sorted) arrays. On an already-sorted array, the pivot is always the minimum element, leaving one partition empty and the other with n-1 elements. This leads to a recurrence relation of T(n) = T(n-1) + O(n), which results in O(n^2) comparisons.
counterexample: The family of sorted arrays A_n = [1, 2, ..., n] for all n >= 1. On A_n, the first element (the minimum) is selected as the pivot, leading to n-1 comparisons during the partition step and subproblems of size 0 and n-1. This behavior repeats for each recursive call on the remaining n-1 elements, resulting in a total of (n-1) + (n-2) + ... + 1 = n(n-1)/2 comparisons. This total is Omega(n^2), which is not O(n log n).
